global_rules.rule: Do not deviate from the procedures described in this document. If a situation arises that is not covered, escalate to the HR Director immediately by posting a notification in Slack with the tag [OUT OF SCOPE] – [email subject line].

The HR Coordinator’s role is administrative and digital – process cases using email, Slack, calendar, Jira, and the reference spreadsheets and document templates. Physical tasks (in‑person orientation, document verification, badge issuance) are performed by the hiring manager or the employee’s supervisor.
All times are Mountain Standard Time (MST, UTC‑7) or Mountain Daylight Time (MDT, UTC‑6). Use MM/DD/YYYY for dates and MM/DD/YYYY HH:MMam/pm for timestamps.
Employee internal email addresses follow the format [first initial].[last name]@crestwood.edu and must be looked up in employee_roster.xlsx before sending any email.
All operational HR communications must use the designated Slack channels; direct messages are prohibited for case‑related communication.
Never rely on memory; always verify employee and case information from the listed source files before taking action.
Every incoming HR request (email, Slack, or in‑person) must be triaged before any action is taken. Internal HR team messages are exempt.
If a single request raises multiple issues, create separate Jira tickets for each issue and apply the highest priority of any individual issue to the whole email for SLA and folder‑routing purposes.
Replies to a previous email are treated as a continuation of the existing case; add the information as a comment to the existing Jira ticket and do not create a new ticket or resend prior templates.
SLA timelines count only business days (Monday‑Friday) and exclude university‑observed holidays.

triage.name: HR Request Triage
steps: Step 1: Verify the requester exists in employee_roster.xlsx or recruiting_tracker.xlsx. If not found, reply using Template 1 and stop.
Step 2: Identify the request category according to Section 7.
Step 3: If the request is an employee‑relations matter (workplace complaint, harassment, discrimination), forward immediately to m.voss@crestwood.edu, reply using Template 2, and stop.
Step 4: If the request involves payroll or compensation, forward to c.briggs@crestwood.edu, reply using Template 3, and stop.
Step 5: Search Jira for an open ticket for the same employee and request type. If found, add the new information as a comment and stop.
Step 6: Create a new Jira ticket using the naming convention in the routing table and assign it per the routing rules.
Step 7: Perform the required action from the relevant SOP section, using the designated email template (Section 18).
Step 8: Complete email housekeeping as described in Section 17, then close the triage.

Leave Management.jira: LEAVE-[Employee Last Name]-[Date request received MMDDYYYY]

Recruiting.jira: RECRUIT-[Requisition ID or Last Name]-[Requisition Approved Date MMDDYYYY]

Employee Relations.jira: ER-[Employee Last Name]-[Complaint Received Date MMDDYYYY]

Benefits & Payroll.jira: BENEFITS-[Employee Last Name]-[Request Received Date MMDDYYYY]

priority.name: Priority Matrix
levels: P1 – Urgent: Compliance deadline within 24 hours, legal or safety issue, employee locked out of pay/benefits. SLA – Same business day.
P2 – High: Compliance deadline within 3 business days, formal complaint, FMLA eligibility determination, PIP‑related termination in progress. SLA – 1 business day.
P3 – Standard: Routine processing with no imminent deadline (standard onboarding/offboarding, evaluation scheduling, PTO balance inquiries). SLA – 3 business days.
P4 – Low: General inquiries, employment verification, policy questions, document requests. SLA – 5 business days.

escalation.name: Escalation Procedure
steps: Post to #hr-escalations for any issue requiring HR Director or VP attention (legal threats, compliance deadlines, unresolved cases >10 business days).

For I‑9 overdue after Day 3, forward the case to n.ashford@crestwood.edu and j.whitfield@crestwood.edu, then post to #hr-escalations with the format: I‑9 OVERDUE: [Employee Name], [Employee ID], Start Date: [MM/DD/YYYY], Deadline: [MM/DD/YYYY].
If a request falls outside the SOP, send a Slack notification to the HR Director with the tag [OUT OF SCOPE] and include the email subject line.
must_not: Do not use direct messages for case‑related communication.
Do not share confidential employee information in public Slack channels.

definitions.FMLA: Family and Medical Leave Act. Federal law entitling eligible employees to up to 12 weeks of unpaid, job‑protected leave per year.
definitions.ADA: Americans with Disabilities Act. Federal law requiring employers to provide reasonable accommodations to qualified employees with disabilities.
definitions.COBRA: Consolidated Omnibus Budget Reconciliation Act. Federal law requiring employers to offer continuation of group health coverage after a qualifying event.
definitions.PIP: Performance Improvement Plan. A formal, documented plan to address and correct employee performance deficiencies.
definitions.I-9: Employment Eligibility Verification form. Federal form required within 3 business days of an employee's first day of work.
definitions.PTO: Paid Time Off. Combined vacation and personal leave accrued by eligible employees.
definitions.Qualifying Event: A life event (marriage, birth, divorce, loss of other coverage) that triggers eligibility for mid‑year benefits enrollment changes or COBRA coverage.
definitions.Exempt Employee: An employee exempt from overtime provisions of the Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA), typically salaried.
definitions.Non-Exempt Employee: An employee entitled to overtime pay under the FLSA, typically hourly.
definitions.Probationary Period: The first 90 calendar days of employment for staff, or the first academic year for faculty.
definitions.Supervisor of Record: The direct supervisor listed in employee_roster.xlsx for a given employee.
definitions.Benefits Enrollment Window: The first 30 calendar days from an employee's start date during which the employee must enroll in or waive benefits.

Open onboarding_checklist.xlsx and create a new row for the employee. All checklist fields must be blank (not started) at this stage.

Post to #hr-onboarding: NEW HIRE: [Employee Name], [Position], [Department], [Campus], Start Date: [MM/DD/YYYY], Jira: [Ticket ID].

Send Template 5 (IT Access Provisioning Request) to j.park@crestwood.edu. Include employee name, position, department, campus, start date, and supervisor name.

Send Template 31 (Orientation Coordinator Request) to the hiring manager. This email instructs the hiring manager to conduct the in‑person orientation on the employee's first day and to collect the I‑9 documents. Attach i9_form.pdf and benefits_enrollment_packet.pdf.
Create a Calendar event titled "Orientation – [Employee Name]" on the employee's first day, 9:00 am–12:00 pm MST.

Steps 4‑7 must be sent/completed before the employee's first day.

procedures.name: FMLA Leave Requests
procedures.applies_when: When an employee submits a request for Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA) leave.

decisions.rule: Hire date ≥ 12 months ago AND Hours Worked ≥ 1,250 in the trailing 12 months

steps: Open employee_roster.xlsx and confirm the employee's hire date.
Calculate the number of months between the hire date and today's date; if fewer than 12 months, mark the employee INELIGIBLE.
Locate the 'Hours Worked (Trailing 12 Months)' column for the employee; if the value is less than 1,250, mark the employee INELIGIBLE.

If ELIGIBLE, send Template 15 (FMLA Eligibility Notice – Approved) to the employee within 5 business days of receiving the request. The employee has 15 calendar days to return the completed medical certification.
Create a Jira ticket named LEAVE-[Last Name]-[MMDDYYYY] where the date is the request‑received date.
Post to Slack channel #hr-leave-requests: "FMLA REQUEST: [Employee Name], [Employee ID], Eligible: YES, Certification Due: [MM/DD/YYYY], Jira: [Ticket ID]".
Create a Calendar reminder titled "FMLA Certification Due – [Employee Name]" on the certification deadline date (15 calendar days after request).
When the medical certification is received, forward it to p.huang@crestwood.edu for review and update leave_tracker.xlsx with the leave dates and status "Approved – Pending Certification Review."
After Patricia Huang approves the certification, update leave_tracker.xlsx status to "Approved," send Template 16 (FMLA Leave Confirmed) to the employee, and CC the supervisor of record.

If INELIGIBLE, send Template 17 (FMLA Eligibility Notice – Denied) to the employee within 5 business days, specifying the reason ("employed for fewer than 12 months," "fewer than 1,250 hours worked," or "both"), and CC Patricia Huang.
Create a Jira ticket named LEAVE-[Last Name]-[MMDDYYYY] and update leave_tracker.xlsx with the request date and status "Denied – [Reason]".
If the employee does not return the medical certification within 15 calendar days, send Template 18 (FMLA Certification Overdue) to the employee.
Post to #hr-leave-requests: "FMLA CERTIFICATION OVERDUE: [Employee Name], [Employee ID], Due: [MM/DD/YYYY], [X] days overdue".
Forward the overdue notice to p.huang@crestwood.edu; Patricia Huang will determine whether the leave is denied or an extension is granted.
deadlines: Eligibility notice (Template 15 or 17) must be sent within 5 business days of receiving the request.
Employee must return the medical certification within 15 calendar days of the eligibility notice.
Calendar reminder is set for the certification due date (15 days after request).
must_not: Do not approve the leave before Patricia Huang reviews and approves the medical certification.
Do not send Template 16 (FMLA Leave Confirmed) before the leave_tracker.xlsx status is updated to "Approved."
notes: Eligibility determination must be completed before any communication is sent to the employee.
All Jira tickets use the format LEAVE-[Last Name]-[MMDDYYYY] to ensure traceability.

procedures.name: Escalations
procedures.applies_when: When a case meets any of the escalation criteria defined in section 16 (P1 issue, unresolved > 10 business days, legal threat, potential harm, or media inquiry).

inputs.fact: Email content indicating legal threat, attorney reference, or regulatory complaint
Email content indicating potential harm to employee or university
Email content indicating a media inquiry related to HR matters

decisions.rule: Email contains legal threat OR reference to attorney OR regulatory complaint
Email contains potential harm to employee OR potential harm to university
Email is a media inquiry related to HR matters

steps: Identify the escalation trigger by evaluating case priority, age, and email content.

If D3 (legal threat) is true: Do NOT reply to the email; post to Slack channel #hr-escalations using format: LEGAL THREAT: [Employee Name], [Subject Line]; forward the original email to hr-escalations@crestwood.edu; Dr. Whitfield and Nicole Ashford will handle further communication.
If D5 (media inquiry) is true: Do NOT reply to the email; forward the email to communications@crestwood.edu (Office of Communications) and to hr-escalations@crestwood.edu.
If any of D1, D2, D4 are true (or after completing D3/D5 steps): Send an escalation notification to the HR Director (Nicole Ashford) indicating the case details and reason for escalation.
deadlines: All escalation actions must be performed immediately (within the same business day the trigger is identified).
must_not: Do NOT reply to the original email when it is a legal threat.
Do NOT reply to the original email when it is a media inquiry.
notes: P1 issues are highest priority and require immediate escalation.
Legal‑threat escalations are routed through Slack #hr-escalations before any email forwarding.
